quarterly_data.signal: Near-term pivotal readouts named by CEO Chris Boerner for the remainder of 2026: admilparant ('a potential first-in-class medicine that could redefine the standard of care in pulmonary fibrosis'), arlo-cel in relapse or refractory multiple myeloma, iberdomide progression-free survival data, milvexian in secondary stroke prevention, RYZ101 in GEP-NETs and Sotyktu in lupus. He said together they 'represent multibillion-dollar peak sales potential.'

quarterly_data.signal: Milvexian atrial fibrillation study status. Chris Boerner said the independent data monitoring committee continues to endorse the study, and that across its reviews BMS has seen 'a slowing of event rates along with the continued view that the efficacy continues to be in line with expectations to continue the study.' Cristian Massacesi said BMS remains blinded, the study is designed for non-inferiority on strokes and systemic embolisms (primary endpoint) and superiority on bleedings (secondary endpoint) and is 'fully designed and powered to show another ratio of 1'; he said 'milvexian can be the first Factor XI drug to be at parity on efficacy with ELIQUIS, but beating ELIQUIS on bleedings.' Adam Lenkowsky said the study was designed to demonstrate a superior bleeding profile compared to ELIQUIS with comparable efficacy.

Admilparant phase II basis for the phase III program. Cristian Massacesi said the phase II results in both IPF and PPF 'were very positive for FVC primary endpoint'; the phase II tested 30 and 60 (the transcript prints 'ml'), with 60 the dose 'showing better and higher benefit', which was carried into phase III, and BMS kept endpoints, population and criteria consistent between phase II and phase III. He said 'we believe that amilparant can be first and best in class against the LPA1.'
